prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker for everyone — the right choice depends on what you need (platform, budget, style, scale). Below is a short, practical guide and recommended options by use case to help you pick quickly.

Quick questions before a specific recommendation
- Which platform(s) are you advertising on (TikTok, Facebook/Instagram, YouTube, display)?  
- Do you need a human presenter/AI avatar, product-focused reels, or animated text/templates?  
- How many variations do you need (one-off vs hundreds for A/B testing)?  
- Budget range and must-have features (voice cloning, script→video, API, no-watermark)?

Top picks by use case (summary)

1) Best for human-presenter/script-to-video (professional, brand-safe)
- Synthesia — realistic AI presenters, many languages, brand controls, easy script→video. Great for product explainers, demo ads, training ads.
- Alternatives: HeyGen / Movio / Elai / Colossyan (similar avatar-driven workflows, different pricing/looks)

2) Best for social short ads & repurposing (fast vertical clips)
- Opus Clip / Vidyo.ai — auto-extracts short social clips from long videos, great for creators/repurposing.
- CapCut (and mobile creators tools) — free, very strong for TikTok-style edits.

3) Best for scalable performance ads / many variants
- Pencil — AI generates ad creatives and predicts performance; built for paid-marketer workflows and multivariants.
- Shakr — templates and scale focused on Facebook/Instagram/TikTok ad production for e-commerce teams.

4) Best for template-based, easy ad creation (speed + affordability)
- InVideo, Promo.com, Biteable — lots of templates, quick editing, good library of music/stock. Good for social and search ads.
- Canva — simple video ad templates, collaborative, lots of assets; good free/low-cost option.

5) Best for advanced editing + voice/over editing
- Descript — superb for editing spoken video, overdub (voice cloning), captions; good for narrative ads and tutorials.
- VEED.IO — simple editor, subtitles, AI text-to-speech, auto-translations.

6) Best for generative visuals / creative experimentation
- Runway — strong generative clips and advanced visual tools if you want unique visuals beyond stock footage.

Other important considerations
- Rights & licensing: Confirm commercial use & music licenses before publishing.  
- Watermarks & resolution: Trial/free tiers often add watermarks or limit resolution.  
- Integrations/APIs: If you need programmatic scale, check for an API or ad-platform integrations.  
- Multi-aspect outputs: Make sure it can export 9:16, 4:5, 16:9 for different placements.

How I’d choose for common scenarios
- Short TikTok ad with a talking product demo and brand avatar: Synthesia or HeyGen.  
- 30–60s Facebook carousel/video ad using product shots + text overlays: Shakr or Promo + Canva.  
- Hundreds of ad variants to test: Pencil (for generation + prediction) + InVideo templates.  
- Repurposing a webinar into dozens of social clips: Opus Clip or Vidyo.ai + Descript for touchups.

If you tell me your platform, ad length, whether you want a human-looking presenter, and your budget, I’ll recommend 2–3 specific tools and a suggested workflow (including sample pricing tiers and whether to test a free trial first).
